10.1002_adfm.202530258: The fast charge–discharge capability of layered oxide cathodes is critical for their practical applications, but their intrinsic 2D structure results in high ionic transport barriers. Herein, we propose a protonation‐induced reconstruction strategy that boosts the effective electric potential by eliminating interfacial and bulk ion‐transport barriers in the NaNi 0.4 Fe 0.2 Mn 0.4 O 2 (NFM) cathode, delivering a comprehensive enhancement in fast‐charging performance. The introduction of Zr(HPO 4 ) 2 as a proton source enables the formation of a functional surface sheltering layer with 3D high‐speed ionic channels on NFM, which effectively removes surface residual alkali and thereby establishes a surface potential field that facilitates ultrafast ion transport. Concurrently, the transition metal–oxygen (TM─O) coordination in the bulk lattice is optimized, with the corresponding bond length shortened. This coordination optimization effectively lowers the internal ion‐transport resistance and shortens the diffusion pathways, enabling rapid bulk ion migration. As a result, the protonated‐reconstructed NFM cathode exhibits a high specific capacity of 94.4 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh rate of 20C. This work provides fundamental insights into potential field engineering of layered oxide cathodes and presents a promising strategy for the design of high‐rate sodium‐ion battery materials.
10.1002_adfm.79269: Zinc‐ferricyanide flow batteries offer low‐cost energy storage, but osmotic water redistribution and the conductivity‐selectivity trade‐off of sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) membranes limit operation at high electrolyte concentrations. Here, an aryl‐sulfonate‐functionalized V 2 CT x /SPEEK interface is engineered to promote cation conduction while limiting ferricyanide crossover and electrolyte redistribution. Tetramethylammonium hydroxide‐assisted redispersion provides thin V 2 C‐SO 3 nanosheets for incorporation into SPEEK. Compared with the unfunctionalized V 2 CT x /SPEEK control, the resulting membrane exhibits higher ionic conductivity, lower swelling and ferricyanide permeability, and reduced electrolyte redistribution during cycling. With a 0.8 M K 3 [Fe(CN) 6 ] catholyte, the optimized membrane retains 81.4% of its initial capacity after 390 cycles and delivers an energy efficiency of 88.9% at cycle 390. At 0.1 M, the cell operates for 7,000 cycles with a capacity‐decay rate of 0.0013% per cycle. The peak power density increases from 691.3 mW cm − 2 for pristine SPEEK to 822.9 mW cm − 2 . These results demonstrate that aryl‐sulfonate functionalization improves the balance between cation transport, dimensional stability, and electrolyte retention in zinc‐ferricyanide flow batteries.
